chunks: I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, among the knowledge that we have been given is the interpretation of the Qur’an, its rulings, and knowledge of the changing of time and its occurrences. When Allah intends good for a people, He causes them to hear; and if He were to make one hear who does not truly hear, he would turn away in aversion as though he had not heard.”
Then he was silent for a short while, then he said: “If we were to find receptacles or a place of rest, we would speak; and Allah is the One whose help is sought.”

key_terms.أَحْكَامَهُ: the Qur’an’s rulings and legal judgments
key_terms.أَوْعِيَةً: receptacles, meaning people capable of preserving knowledge
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعَانُ: the One whose help is sought
key_terms.تَفْسِيرَ الْقُرْآنِ: the interpretation and explanation of the Qur’an
key_terms.حَدَثَانِهِ: its newly occurring events and developments
key_terms.عِلْمِ: divinely granted knowledge possessed by the Imams

ai.seo_question: What knowledge did Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) say the Imams possess?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) states that the Ahl al-Bayt possess divinely granted knowledge, including the interpretation of the Qur’an, its rulings, and awareness of changing times and events. He also teaches that receptivity to truth is a divine grace, and indicates that fuller knowledge requires worthy and trustworthy people to receive it.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Qasim Bin Al Rabie, from Ubeyd Bin Abdullah Bin Abu Hashim Al Sayrafi, from Amro Bin Mus’ab, from Salma Bin Muhriz who said, 
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘From the Knowledge which we<sup>asws</sup> have been Given is the interpretation of the Quran, and its Judgments, and knowledge of the changing of times and its new occurrences. Whenever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Intends good with a people, He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes them to listen, and if someone hears whom He<sup>azwj</sup> Does not Want him to hear, he would turn around as if he had not heard’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> waited for a while, then said: ‘If we<sup>asws</sup> were to find a retaining ear or a receptacle, we<sup>asws</sup> would say (tell all), and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Aider’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Qasim ibn al-Rabi‘ from ‘Ubayd ibn ‘Abdallah ibn abu Hashim al-Sayrafi from ‘Amr ibn Mus‘ab from Salma ibn Muhriz who has said that he heard abu Ja‘far (a.s.) say the following. “Of the knowledge that we have received is the interpretation of the Holy Quran and its laws, the knowledge of the changes of time and the happenings therein. When Allah wants good for a people, He makes them to understand. If He would make to understand one who does not want to understand such a person turns away as if he has heard nothing.
The Imams (a.s.) paused, briefly, then said, “Had we found keepers and trusted people for our knowledge, we would have said it (all to him). Allah is the best supporter.”
